program.title: 5K Running Foundation – Week 1
program.goal: Build aerobic base and lower-leg capacity for 5K running with run-walk tolerance and pain-free progression

athlete_analysis.profile_summary: Beginner 5K runner, 1 session/week outdoors, previous shin soreness. Needs run-walk foundation, calf/soleus capacity work, and conservative load progression.
primary_constraints: Previous shin soreness: avoid high-impact volume spikes, prioritize soleus strength
1 session/week: must integrate run + strength in single 45-min session
Outdoors only: bodyweight and minimal equipment focus
sport_demands: Lower-leg tissue capacity and ankle stability
athlete_analysis.block_priority: Establish consistent run-walk habit, build soleus/calf endurance, and monitor 24-hour shin response before advancing intensity or volume.

weeks.theme: Introduce run-walk intervals with embedded single-leg calf strength

workouts.title: Run-Walk + Lower-Leg Strength
sport_transfer: Impact tolerance via controlled run-walk intervals
Calf/soleus capacity supports running economy and shin resilience
Single-leg strength transfers to running balance and propulsion
workouts.why_this_session: Run-walk builds aerobic base with low shin stress. Strength work targets soleus (bent-knee calf) and single-leg control to durably support running load.

warmup.name: Glute Bridge
warmup.purpose: Activate glutes and hips, reinforce posterior pelvic tilt before running

warmup.name: Bird Dog
warmup.purpose: Stabilize core and low back without loading spine vertically

warmup.name: Dead Bug
warmup.purpose: Build trunk control and anti-extension awareness for upright running posture

main_work.name: Run-Walk Intervals
main_work.purpose: Build aerobic base and impact tolerance using run-walk pattern to manage shin load
main_work.duration: 20 min total (start 2 min jog / 1 min walk, repeat 5 cycles or adjust by feel)

main_work.name: Seated Calf Raise
main_work.purpose: Build soleus endurance and calf capacity in bent-knee position (lower eccentric stress on shin)
main_work.load_guidance: Bodyweight or light plate on thighs if available; focus on full stretch and full raise
main_work.tempo: 2 sec up, 1 sec pause, 2 sec down

main_work.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise
main_work.purpose: Develop unilateral ankle stability and single-leg calf strength for running balance and propulsion
main_work.load_guidance: Light dumbbell or wall support for balance; prioritize control over reps
main_work.tempo: 2 sec up, 1 sec pause, 2 sec down

main_work.name: Step-Up
main_work.purpose: Build single-leg hip and knee control, strengthen lead-leg extensors for running stride
main_work.load_guidance: Knee-high step or low bench, bodyweight; emphasize full foot contact and upright posture
main_work.tempo: 2 sec up, 1 sec pause, 2 sec down

cooldown.name: Soleus Wall Stretch
cooldown.purpose: Static stretch soleus with bent knee to maintain ankle dorsiflexion range and reduce shin tension

cooldown.name: Knee-to-Wall Ankle Rocks
cooldown.purpose: Dynamic ankle dorsiflexion mobility to improve running mechanics and landing position

injury_modifications: If shin pain appears during run-walk, reduce jog duration and increase walk breaks (1:1 or even 1:2 ratio); re-assess after 48 hours before progressing
Seated Calf Raise and Single-Leg Calf Raise are low-impact alternatives to standing calf work; if Achilles pain appears, reduce range or remove single-leg variant
Stop immediately if pain worsens during or 24 hours after session; consult medical guidance before next week

weeks.progression_rule: Complete 20 min run-walk at RPE 5-6 (easy conversation pace, walk breaks as needed). Assess 24-hour shin response; if stable, progress run:walk ratio next week.

program.nutrition_focus: Maintain consistent carbohydrate intake around easy runs and strength work (e.g., light snack 30–60 min before session); hydrate normally based on outdoor conditions.
recovery_focus: Sleep 7+ hours nightly to support aerobic adaptation and tissue repair
Monitor 24-hour shin response after session; stable or improving pain allows progression; worsening pain triggers regress or hold
Break up sitting with 5–10 min mobility snacks (hip, ankle, thoracic) on non-training days
safety_notes: Previous shin soreness is a primary constraint; avoid rapid volume or intensity spikes; run-walk format with embedded low-impact strength is safest entry
No true 1RM tests or max sprints this week; all work is foundational aerobic and mobility-supported
Outdoor terrain and footwear consistency matter; avoid changing shoes or running surface suddenly mid-week
assumptions: Athlete has medical clearance for running; previous shin soreness is resolved but warrants conservative re-entry
1 session/week is sole dedicated training day; assumed athlete recovers from normal daily activity
Bodyweight and minimal equipment (wall, bench, light dumbbells if available) are realistic given outdoors-only location
RPE-based intensity assumes athlete can self-assess easy (5–6) vs. moderate (6–7) effort
Run-walk ratio (2:1, 1:1, etc.) will adapt weekly based on pain response and completion feedback
